data.description:
`bridge_fsck` reads `prev_snapshot.json` off disk as its offline Jira oracle and uses the **field
values**, so narrowing prev to a key-set (A4-2) would silently degrade its drift classification.
Fence it first. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why first
`bridge_fsck.py:306-308` loads the file as `jira_snapshot` and passes `fields=jira_snapshot[key]`
into `ObservedJira.PRESENT` at `:344` and `:380`. With `{}` entries, membership still works but
every field-based classification degrades. This is an **out-of-band consumer of the file itself**, not
of `ctx.prev_snapshot`, so no test that exercises `reconcile_once` would catch it. It reads the
**working tree**, so it is unaffected by clone filters.

## Approach
Make the field-dependence explicit: classify on membership where that is sufficient, and where a
field value is genuinely required, report the classification as **indeterminate** rather than
inferring from an empty dict. Do not silently treat absent fields as absent values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Against a **key-set** prev fixture (`{jira_key: {}}`), `bridge_fsck` drift classification is
      identical to its classification against the equivalent full-payload fixture for every case that
      does not require a field value, and reports **indeterminate** (never a false drift) for cases
      that do. Tier: **unit** with paired fixtures.
- [ ] Against a full-payload prev, behaviour is byte-identical to today (no regression for the
      pre-A4-2 world). Tier: **unit** golden comparison.
- [ ] `rebar bridge-fsck` exit code and JSON shape are unchanged for both fixtures. Tier: **CLI
      subprocess**.

## Files
`src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py`, tests

Scope: S. No dependencies (independent of A1/A2/A3).
data.title: A4-1: fence bridge_fsck's offline drift oracle before prev_snapshot is narrowed
